h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, י״ז Ki Savo, 17
The Seven Consolations Descend From Above and Rise From Below

p: is a preparation for Rosh Hashanah,
as they said in the Gemara (Megillah 31b):
"so that the year may end with its curses";
is already "let the year begin with its blessings"
And therefore on this Shabbos they read as haftarah
"Arise, shine, for your light has come";
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד)
and this is based on what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4):
for on Rosh Hashanah is the coming-into-being of the light.
Now the matter of the seven haftaros of consolation:
and afterward "And Tziyon said, Hashem has forsaken me";
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָנֹכִי אָנֹכִי הוּא מְנַחֶמְכֶם
and afterward "I, I am He who comforts you."
that the seven haftaros of consolation
correspond to the seven attributes of the structure,
and the order is from above to below;
for first Hashem, may He be blessed, clarifies
in the three Shabbosos of calamity,
and afterward, in the seven of consolation,
Hashem, may He be blessed, clarifies Yisrael
for which the seven shepherds are a chariot.
And it says in the first,
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט, ב)
and this is in the manner of what they said (Shabbos 89b):
"If your sins be like these years,
which have been ordered and come
since the six days of Creation,
they shall be made white as snow" (Yeshayahu 1:18)
that is, that intentional sins become like merits;
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
וְנִתְבַּשֵּׂר לְךָ טַל יַלְדוּתֶךָ (תְּהִלִּים קי, ג)
and he was given the tidings, "yours is the dew of your youth" (Tehillim 110:3);
corresponding to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַפְטוֹרַת עֲנִיָּה סוֹעֲרָה (שָׁם נד, יא)
And afterward the haftarah "O afflicted, storm-tossed one" (ibid. 54:11),
and it is expounded in the Pesikta:
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
שֶׁאָמַר מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי (תְּהִלִּים קכא, א)
who said, "From where will my help come?" (Tehillim 121:1)
this is the consolation through words of Torah,
for the beginning of the Ten Commandments
and this corresponds to Moshe Rabbeinu,
who brought the Torah down from heaven.
are from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed.
who is the groomsman of the Queen,
"and draws them near to the Torah" (Avos 1:12).
for the main spread of words of Torah
was in the exile of Bavel;
and this corresponds to the attribute of Hod,
for which Aharon HaKohen is a chariot.
which corresponds to the attribute of Hod,
as written in the holy Zohar
and the sealing of the Babylonian Talmud,
which is the essence of the Oral Torah,
and most of the great Rishonim;
and this is "Sing, O barren one," in the present.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ בַּה׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, י)
And afterward, "I will greatly rejoice in Hashem" (Yeshayahu 61:10),
corresponding to the attribute of Malchus;
which is when one merits being of upright heart,
"and for the upright of heart, joy" (Tehillim 97:11)
(as written at the end of the chapter in Taanis);
and this corresponds to the light of Mashiach,
who will be "the individual who repents,
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven";
are from the side of Yisrael,
and they are in the present.

p: the order of these seven haftaros
from below to above as well;
corresponding to which are the three of calamity,
Yisrael are clarified from their own side
And it begins in the first,
speak to the heart of Yerushalayim,"
which alludes to the attribute of Malchus;
and it says, "for her iniquity is pardoned"
that is, Hashem, may He be blessed, promises
that afterward they will be like merits,
and this is that the supernal Crown
alludes to the attribute of Yesod;
for the main purpose of the exiles,
it is brought from the holy Arizal,
is to rectify the blemish of the covenant;
and Tziyon has the numerical value of Yosef.
And this is "And Tziyon said, Hashem has forsaken me":
for they see that much time has passed
and it has not yet been completely rectified;
כִּי נִחַם ה׳ צִיּוֹ״ן (יְשַׁעְיָה נא, ג)
which is the attribute of "tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
for which Yosef is a chariot.
whose occupation was mainly the avodah;
and in exile "there is no one who seeks,"
and we have no avodah of the offerings.
which open with "I am Hashem your God,"
And it begins with "Sing, O barren one,"
corresponding to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
that is, whoever is only of his seed,
לֹא יוּכַל לַעֲקוֹר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ
the name Yisrael cannot be uprooted from him,
And this is what it says,
"Sing, O barren one who did not bear";
as among the nations of the world
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
who is a chariot for the attribute of Gevurah,
And it is brought in the Tikkunim
and this is the second arm,
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד)
and it is brought in Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4),
And afterward the haftarah "I will greatly rejoice"
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who is the essential purpose of the creation of the world,
and it is written, "when they were created" (Bereishis 2:4),
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יב, ט)
and it is brought in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 12:9)
And Shabbos includes all seven attributes
therefore they read these haftaros on the Shabbosos,
